confidence.rationale: The restaurant-issued homepage directly confirms extensive current Lunch, Dinner, and Brunch menus, explicit ingredient positives, extraction artifacts, and the absence of allergen or cross-contact disclosures. Terra's core discrepancy is supported, although one PDF and several deterministic counts were overstated.

confirmedFindings: The packet contains 56 affected baseline items: 44 implicated in overstated allergen authority and 16 in extraction artifacts or collisions, with four items overlapping those sets.

All 97 baseline records were reconciled: 54 exact_match/mismatch, 14 variant_match/mismatch, 11 exact_match/accurately_unavailable, 2 normalized_match/mismatch, 2 variant_match/accurately_unavailable, 4 stale_extra/not_applicable, and 10 artifact/not_applicable.
The official homepage currently exposes substantial Lunch, Dinner, and Brunch catalogs, contradicting Luna's zero-current-product result.
Dish descriptions are not complete ingredient or allergen specifications. They cannot establish complete allergen arrays, allergen negatives, may-contain claims, or cross-contact conclusions.

Restaurant-issued explicit positives remain valid narrowly: examples include milk from named cream cheese, parmigiano, mozzarella, feta, butter, or stracciatella; shellfish from named shrimp, crab, lobster, clams, mussels, or oysters; fish from named tuna, swordfish, halibut, sole, or salmon; egg from explicitly named eggs or egg white; and tree nuts from named cashews or almond paste.

The frozen baseline contains genuine duplicate, variant, misspelled, and non-product records, including Bolognaise/Bolognese, Chicken Paillard/Paillarp, duplicate pancakes, description fragments, pricing text, and carousel text.
No restaurant-issued shared-equipment or cross-contact disclosure was found. The raw-or-undercooked-food warning is unrelated and cannot support a cross-contact conclusion.

Count drift, partial non-exact reconciliation, incomplete authority, low confidence, and scout risk are substantiated in principle, but several deterministic metrics are not reliable as literal current counts.

Rejected any interpretation of crossContactCount=1 as evidence that cross-contact exists. Available primary sources establish only that cross-contact information is unavailable.
Rejected treating Terra's ten additional-current-product records as a complete current catalog; Terra did not comprehensively enumerate current products and unresolved PDF presentations remain.

Rejected wholesale removal of valid positive allergen evidence. Unsupported completeness and negatives must be removed, while explicit restaurant-issued ingredients and unavoidable named identities retain narrow positive support.
Rejected culinary-assumption expansion beyond explicit wording or unavoidable identity; preparation conventions alone cannot add allergens.
